title: At a Restaurant
description: Learn how to order food, ask for the bill, and navigate a Tamil restaurant conversation.

exercises.explanation: Restaurant essentials — these four words will get you through most dining situations in Tamil Nadu.

exercises.question: How do you ask for the bill in Tamil?
exercises.explanation: 'Bill kodunga' = please bring the bill. 'Kodunga' is the polite form of 'give'.
'Enakku saadam saapida vendum' = I want to eat rice. Or simply 'saadam kodunga' (give me rice).
exercises.hint: sounds like: en-nuk-ku saa-dum saa-pi-da ven-dum

exercises.explanation: 'Romba ruchi!' = very delicious! — ruchi = delicious/tasty, romba = very. A great compliment to a cook.
'Ruchi' means delicious or tasty — saying 'romba ruchi' (very tasty) will make any cook happy.

exercises.question: How do you ask for one more dosai?
exercises.explanation: 'Innum onnu dosai kodunga' = please give one more dosai. Innum = more/another, onnu = one.
'Oru kaapi kodunga' = please give one coffee. Oru = one, kodunga = please give.
'Veg saapadu irukka?' = do you have vegetarian food? A very common question in Tamil Nadu.
